news.title: B轮融资总额上升，但交易数量减少
news.snippet: 分析显示B轮融资金额增长，但完成交易数量下降，市场更趋集中。
news.raw_snippet:
Meanwhile, one of the least surprising findings from our analysis of Series B recipients is that it was a heavily AI-focused group.

So far this year, about two-thirds of Series B funding has gone to AI-focused startups, per Crunchbase data. In 2025, by comparison, about half of investment went to companies in AI categories.

AI companies were also heavily represented by round count. So far in 2026, more than half of all reported U.S. Series B deals have been for AI companies. [...] At least 110 companies have raised rounds of $100 million or more around this stage so far this year. That’s roughly a quarter of all deals.

Of these, the largest by far was a $12 billion round 3 for Prometheus, Jeff Bezos’ physical AI startup that launched last year. [...] Even so, these don’t look like the best of times for startups seeking smaller Series B rounds. Seems like in the current AI-driven cycle, investors are increasingly focused on big checks for high-valuation companies.

news.title: Anthropic IPO谁会受益
news.snippet: 聊天机器人制造商Anthropic提交备受期待的S-1招股书，投资者与早期股东或将获利。
news.raw_snippet:
The release of the chatbot maker’s highly anticipated S-1 helped prompt a rebound in tech stocks on Monday. The prospectus laid out the promises, challenges and risks of commercializing cutting-edge A.I., with some eye-popping numbers. That said, it left out key details.

Analysts and bettors on Polymarket, the prediction market, are left to speculate on whether Anthropic will hit a $2 trillion valuation, a number that Wall Street and Silicon Valley have been buzzing about for months. [...] One major standout? Spark Capital. It is poised to turn its approximately $777 million in investments made since 2023 into a staggering $10.9 billion if Anthropic achieves a $1.5 trillion valuation, according to PitchBook. More below.

## The Anthropic effect

The positive vibes around Anthropic’s I.P.O. filing continue to lift markets. U.S. stock futures are gaining on Tuesday even as investors refocus on the huge spending needed to finance the artificial intelligence boom. [...] But the big question is whether Anthropic’s gargantuan listing can reinvigorate the stalled I.P.O. pipeline and squelch A.I. bubble talk.

news.title: AI巨头融资雄心考验华尔街风险偏好
news.snippet: 大型AI公司推进巨额融资计划，考验华尔街对高风险投资的承受能力与兴趣。
news.raw_snippet:
By pressing ahead with their enormous funding plans, the biggest AI players are wagering that investors' fear of missing out on future returns will outweigh their fear of overpaying for them.

AI stocks accounted for nearly 75% of the S&P 500 index's return in the first half of 2026, according to an analysis by Carson Group. [...] Anthropic revealed paperwork for its initial public offering on Monday, paving the way for a share sale reportedly worth $100 billion as early as next month.

Meta also unveiled a plan this week that could bring it as much as $97.5 billion through equity offerings over the coming months.

The markets will also await signs of fundraising plans when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings later on Wednesday. [...] Meta's shares have fallen more than 11% since it unveiled plans last week to create a new class of stock to fund share sales and reported its first quarterly cash burn in more than a decade.

While Anthropic's soaring revenue helped ease AI growth concerns, its mounting losses have raised fresh questions. The company's net loss widened to $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026 from $13 billion a year earlier.

Phil Wahba
Phil Wahba
Etsy logo at company headquarters in Brooklyn on August 5, 2026.

Etsy’s new CEO is fighting a flood of AI-generated junk with a surprising weapon: more AI. [...] Etsy sellers have had enough too. They’ve complained about AI-supported listings, saying such listings often outrank their original offerings in search results and undercut them on price. Many sellers have left the site.

Etsy named Kruti Patel Goyal as CEO at the start of 2026 to try to stop the bleeding, and she’s making some early progress.

news.raw_snippet: Smart Supply Chain hosts Shireen and Sarah Garrison welcome Cynthia Hutchison, Founder and CEO of Gain Group, for a discussion on connecting people, technology, and innovation to improve supply chain performance. Drawing on decades of industry leadership and experience with the World Economic Forum, Hutchison shares insights on AI adoption, lessons from COVID-era disruptions, supplier collaboration, and workforce development. [...] Artificial intelligence is transforming supply chains, but technology alone isn’t enough. Building smarter, more resilient operations requires human expertise, stronger supplier relationships, and collaboration. [...] The conversation offers fresh perspectives on why human intelligence and stronger connections across the supply chain remain essential to accelerating innovation and building resilience.
